# Complementary quadrilateral incidence in the two-full/one-zero tetrahedral case

This is a necessary-structure theorem for a least-active positive-weight stochastic capacity maximum. It does not settle the remaining configuration.

Consider d=3 and exactly three nonzero rows: two full rows x,y and one row z with exactly one zero, at column h. Let b be the common actual section centroid of the full rows, and suppose b_h>1/3. The zero-row derivative restriction gives b_j<=1/3 for j!=h. By the joint positive-index theorem, the only remaining case has one full row strictly capturing h and the other strictly excluding it. Label x as the capturing row.

All full-row thresholds are unique, proper and nondegenerate by the audited regularity and Schur sources. Set

    t_x=b dot x, t_y=b dot y, t_z=b dot z,
    c^x=t_x 1-x, c^y=t_y 1-y.

The positive-coordinate derivative equations of the one-zero row give, for a single w>0,

    z_h=0,       z_j=w/b_j (j!=h),       t_z=3w.

Since x+y+z=1 componentwise and sum b=1,

    c^x_h+c^y_h=-3w<0,
    c^x_j+c^y_j=w(1/b_j-3)>=0 (j!=h).               (1)

## 1. The capturing row is a strict quadrilateral cut

A proper minimizing full-row cut strictly captures at least two vertices. If its section is triangular, orient the section toward the isolated vertex. Its three section vertices lie on the three incident edges. Every centroid coordinate except the isolated vertex coordinate is an edge-intercept parameter divided by three and is therefore at most 1/3. A boundary vertex has coordinate exactly 1/3. Consequently a triangular section whose centroid coordinate b_h exceeds 1/3 must isolate h. The orientation capturing h then strictly captures only h, which is impossible for the full-row minimum.

Thus x has a strict quadrilateral section and captures exactly {h,j} for one j!=h. Call the other two columns l,m. Since c^x_l,c^x_m<0, equation (1) forces c^y_l,c^y_m>0. The row y excludes h. Its only remaining alternatives are:

- c^y_j<0: a strict complementary quadrilateral cut;
- c^y_j>=0: a triangular section isolating h, with a possible boundary vertex j.

## 2. The triangular alternative is incompatible with the columns

Suppose y has that triangular section. Put

    V=27 product_(j!=h)b_j.

The vertex-h cap has edge intercepts 3b_j and volume fraction V. Scale its raw margin to have value -r at h and values r[1/(3b_j)-1] at j!=h for the complementary y cap, with r>0. The y cap fraction is 1-V and its exponential density at zero is V/r (apply the one-positive-phase formula to the reversed cap). Hence its capacity threshold is r(1-V)/V, and its row is exactly

    y_h=L,       y_j=L[1-V/(3b_j)] (j!=h),          (2)

where L=r/V>0. This calculation includes b_j=1/3 and the corresponding zero raw margin.

Column sums with the displayed z give

    x_h=1-L,
    x_j=1-L+c/b_j (j!=h),   c=LV/3-w.

Taking the b average yields t_x=1-L+3c. Its raw margins are therefore

    c^x_h=3c,
    c^x_j=c(3-1/b_j) (j!=h).                         (3)

Since x strictly captures h, c>0. Every other margin in (3) is nonpositive, because b_j<=1/3. Thus x strictly captures only h, contradicting proper full-row threshold stationarity. The triangular alternative is impossible.

We conclude that BOTH minimizing sections are strict quadrilaterals and their captured vertex pairs are complementary: x captures {h,j} and y captures {l,m}. All boundary-contact alternatives have been excluded by exact formulas, not by perturbation or general position.

## 3. What the equations additionally retain

Define the raw vertex-h cap margin

    m_h(h)=3,       m_h(j)=3-1/b_j (j!=h).

Equation (1) is the exact vector identity

    c^x+c^y=-w m_h.                                 (4)

Thus the two actual quadrilateral section normals and the actual vertex-h section normal have a positive three-term balance. Both quadrilateral planes have centroid b; the vertex-h plane does too. This is stronger than merely requiring equal centroid data for two independent cuts.

It is not legitimate to infer that the two quadrilateral planes coincide. The section-centroid map can have multiple preimages even on one fixed two-versus-two incidence class. Nor is a negative cap Hessian along an arbitrary pair automatically fundable. The remaining task is to use the joint identity (4), or the weighted optimized Hessians including the zero-row curvature, to rule out or pay this genuinely coupled configuration.


## 4. Subsequent exact closure of this stratum

The positive normal pencil in (4) is now classified in `candidate 558c9d47421b8323`: its two central coordinates l,m must agree. The exact simultaneously funded Hessian theorem in `candidate 07a18d1e8e33ee50` then gives a strict feasible improvement. Thus this necessary-structure note now feeds a complete exclusion of the two-full/one-zero stratum; the general (OC) problem and other ordinary capacity strata remain separate.
